answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow accrual: each agent locks a refundable deposit and earns trust only through verified work over time, like tending an orchard rather than planting seeds overnight. A new identity starts with near-zero weight, so thousands of fake agents cost deposits plus months of history. A verifier samples behavior across a canyon of independent tasks for consistency, and an opal-like attestation ledger makes past misconduct visible to all. An attacker must pay real capital and time per identity, while honest agents reuse one reputation cheaply.
